events.summary: Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation is reportedly in early talks to acquire the Los Angeles Times and Chicago Tribune from the Tribune Company.
News Corporation, led by Rupert Murdoch, is due to officially complete its $5bn acquisition of Dow Jones, owner of the Wall Street Journal, with a shareholder vote formalizing the deal.
Rupert Murdoch's 21st Century Fox is pushing for an attempted $80bn acquisition of Time Warner.

Rupert Murdoch met with Sunday Telegraph editor Patience Wheatcroft, Times editor Robert Thomson, and Times business editor James Harding in New York, amid reports that Thomson is being lined up to edit the Wall Street Journal if Murdoch succeeds in his bid to acquire Dow Jones.
Rupert Murdoch celebrates News Corporation's acquisition of the Wall Street Journal with a $2m global advertising campaign.
Rupert Murdoch closes down the News of the World for good amid phone hacking revelations.
Rupert Murdoch met with the Bancroft family, the controlling shareholders of Dow Jones, in a four-hour meeting that was seen as a positive step toward his $5bn takeover bid.
Rupert Murdoch said he aims to make $100m in savings at Dow Jones following News Corporation's acquisition of the company.
Dow Jones shareholders formally approve Rupert Murdoch's bid to acquire the company.
Rupert Murdoch confirms the appointment of his son James Murdoch as chairman and chief executive of News Corporation in Europe and Asia, and Les Hinton as chief executive of Dow Jones.
Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation acquired The Brooklyn Newspaper, which has five free suburban editions, for an undisclosed price.
President George W. Bush appoints former Presidents George H.W. Bush and Bill Clinton to launch a joint appeal for emergency donations to victims of the Indian Ocean tsunami.
Rupert Murdoch confirms that his new standalone publishing group will retain the News Corporation name, with the film and TV businesses to form a separate company named Fox Group.

Rupert Murdoch promises News Corporation will increase its presence in Europe despite the collapse of its relationship with the Kirch Group, while ruling out further investment in Kirch as it currently exists.
Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation-owned newspaper The Australian begins carrying a daily branded Wall Street Journal page in its business section under a partnership deal.

Media Matters for America publishes a full-page ad in the International Herald Tribune criticizing News Corporation and calling on James Murdoch to reform the company, invoking Rupert Murdoch as the representative of the old News Corp.
Rupert Murdoch's News Limited made a A$2bn bid to acquire Consolidated Media Holdings, aiming to double its stake in Foxtel to 50% and Fox Sports to 100%, pending regulatory approval.
Rupert Murdoch appoints his son James as a non-executive director on the BSkyB board, boosting his family's presence on the board of the UK's largest pay TV broadcaster.

A YouGov poll commissioned by Avaaz found that almost 60% of British people believe Rupert Murdoch has too much political influence and 64% believe a full News Corporation takeover of BSkyB would give him too much power over the media.

Rupert Murdoch outlined plans for News Corporation to invest an additional $1bn in online properties and disclosed that the company is in advanced negotiations to acquire a controlling stake in a search engine.
MySpace, owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation, plans to expand into Europe using Britain as a beachhead, with 11 countries earmarked including France and Germany.
Rupert Murdoch reiterated his belief that internet users will pay for news content and criticized news aggregation as "theft" in an address to US media regulators.
President George W. Bush appoints former Presidents George H.W. Bush and Bill Clinton to launch a joint appeal for emergency donations to victims of the Indian Ocean tsunami.
Rupert Murdoch celebrated his 81st birthday.
Rupert Murdoch gave his first British interview in five years, defending his legacy and complaining about resentment from the BBC and establishment forces.
Rupert Murdoch's third wife, Wendi Deng, gave birth to a daughter, Grace, making Murdoch a father for the fifth time at age 70.
Rupert Murdoch said at News Corporation's annual general meeting that his retirement plans had been put on hold "forever" and that he would have to be "carried out."
No single completed or planned topic-related event is specified; the article presents predictions for Rupert Murdoch’s possible 2014 actions.

Rupert Murdoch falls to his lowest ranking in the MediaGuardian 100, attributed to his completed $5.6bn takeover of Wall Street Journal parent company Dow Jones and his focus on the US financial paper.

Rupert Murdoch faced down dissident shareholders at News Corp's annual meeting, defeating proposals for an independent chairman and an end to the dual-class share structure, though a majority of independent shareholders voted for separating the chief executive and chairman roles.
President George W. Bush appoints former Presidents George H.W. Bush and Bill Clinton to lead a joint appeal for emergency donations to victims of the Indian Ocean tsunami.
Hermes Equity Ownership Services advises clients to withhold support from five News Corp directors, including Rupert Murdoch, at the company's annual meeting.
President George W. Bush appoints former Presidents George H.W. Bush and Bill Clinton to launch a joint appeal for emergency donations to victims of the Indian Ocean tsunami.

The National Association of Pension Funds backs Rupert Murdoch’s election of his son James Murdoch to the BSkyB board but calls for the ouster of Lord St John of Fawsley and recommends rejecting BSkyB’s remuneration policy.

facts.text: On 2002-06-20, Rupert Murdoch vowed to stay at the helm of his media empire until he was 100 years old.
On 2003-12-22, Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation completed a £3.8bn deal to acquire DirecTV, giving it control of the largest US satellite pay-TV company.
On 2006-12-22, Rupert Murdoch finalised a deal with John Malone under which News Corp would buy back Malone's 16.3% stake, strengthening Murdoch's control of News Corporation.
On 2007-04-04, News Corp shareholders overwhelmingly approved an $11bn asset swap increasing Rupert Murdoch's control, lifting the Murdoch family's stake to 38% from 31%.
On 2007-12-15, Dow Jones shareholders formally approved Rupert Murdoch's bid to acquire the company, after News Corp was due to complete the $5bn deal on 2007-12-13.
On 2011-07-07, Rupert Murdoch closed down the News of the World for good amid phone hacking revelations.
On 2013-04-17, Rupert Murdoch announced that the entertainment division of News Corporation would be named 21st Century Fox when the company split into two.

On 2013-07-01, Rupert Murdoch's media empire officially split into two separately listed companies: News Corp (newspapers, books, Australian pay-TV) and 21st Century Fox (film, TV, European and Asian pay-TV).

events.summary: The European Commission unconditionally approved 21st Century Fox's £11.7bn bid, backed by Rupert Murdoch, to take full control of Sky.
Culture secretary Karen Bradley is due to deliver her verdict this week on whether to clear 21st Century Fox's proposed £11.7bn takeover of Sky or refer it to competition authorities.
British broadcaster Sky agrees to an £11.2bn takeover by Rupert Murdoch’s US media group 21st Century Fox.
UK Culture Secretary Karen Bradley referred 21st Century Fox's £11.7bn bid for Sky to Ofcom to investigate public interest concerns over media plurality and broadcasting standards.
Rupert Murdoch's 21st Century Fox agrees in principle to an £11.2bn offer to take full control of Sky, five years after a similar bid was abandoned amid the phone-hacking scandal.

Former Labour leader Ed Miliband and ex-business secretary Vince Cable submitted arguments to Ofcom urging it to block Rupert Murdoch’s £11.7bn bid to take over Sky, claiming it would give him too much control of UK news media and that he is not a “fit and proper” owner.

Labour tables an urgent question in parliament about Rupert Murdoch's bid to take full control of Sky, with the government facing 10 working days to decide whether to issue a public interest intervention notice.

UK culture secretary Karen Bradley said she is "minded to" refer Rupert Murdoch's £11.7bn takeover bid for Sky to Ofcom over media plurality and broadcasting standards concerns, but has not made a final decision.
Rupert Murdoch’s 21st Century Fox formally lodged an £11.7bn bid to take full control of Sky.

Rupert Murdoch's 21st Century Fox is planning to use a "scheme of arrangement" for its £11.2bn takeover of Sky, requiring 75% approval from non-Fox shareholders to force out opponents, while facing investor calls to raise the offer price.
Rupert Murdoch's 21st Century Fox is expected to table a formal offer for Sky as soon as Thursday.

Rupert Murdoch's 21st Century Fox is not expected to offer Sky News as a regulatory concession in its £11.2bn takeover bid for Sky, despite having done so during a previous acquisition attempt in 2011.
Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation is close to a deal worth up to $7bn to secure a 35% stake in Hughes Corporation, parent company of US satellite broadcaster DirecTV.
Rupert Murdoch finalised a deal with John Malone under which News Corp will buy back Malone's 16.3% stake, strengthening Murdoch's control of News Corporation.
Rupert Murdoch said due diligence was delaying a planned merger involving News Corporation’s Sky Global Networks and DirecTV parent Hughes Electronics.
Rupert Murdoch is close to a deal to merge his satellite television operations with DirecTV, creating a $70bn business.
Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation completed a £3.8bn deal to acquire DirecTV, giving it control of the largest US satellite pay-TV company.
Rupert Murdoch defended News Corporation’s bid for DirecTV, saying it offered a healthy premium for shareholders.
Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation agrees a $6.6bn deal to take control of Hughes Electronics, parent company of DirecTV.

Rupert Murdoch's News Corp agreed to acquire General Motors' 34 per cent stake in Hughes Electronics, owner of DirecTV, with a termination fee of up to $300m payable to News Corp if the deal fails to close under certain circumstances.
Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation reportedly held secret talks with DirecTV advisers about a potential $30 billion merger.
US regulators are set to approve News Corp's takeover of DirecTV, likely with conditions to limit Rupert Murdoch's market influence.
Rupert Murdoch's 21st Century Fox is pushing for an attempted $80bn acquisition of Time Warner.
Rupert Murdoch appoints Chase Carey as deputy chairman, president, and chief operating officer of News Corp, replacing Peter Chernin as his second in command.

Rupert Murdoch is preparing to step down as chief executive of 21st Century Fox, handing the role to his youngest son James, in a reorganization expected to be ratified at a board meeting as early as next week.
Rupert Murdoch said Peter Chernin would probably succeed him as chief executive of News Corporation, while indicating his children were not yet ready to take his place.

Rupert Murdoch confirmed he will stand down as chief executive of 21st Century Fox at the end of the month, handing over control to his son James, with the management changes approved by the company's board.
A leading pension fund group joins the row over BSkyB's future by demanding answers over Rupert Murdoch's plans to install his youngest son, James, as the company's new chief executive.
President George W. Bush appoints former Presidents George H.W. Bush and Bill Clinton to launch a joint appeal for emergency donations to victims of the Indian Ocean tsunami.

Rupert Murdoch's media empire officially split into two separately listed companies, with the newspaper and book publishing arms and Australian pay-TV assets retaining the News Corp name, while the Fox film and TV businesses and European and Asian pay-TV operations became 21st Century Fox.
Rupert Murdoch is not stepping down at 21st Century Fox, while son James steps up as CEO and son Lachlan joins as executive co-chairman in a partnership arrangement.
Dissident shareholders from the US, UK and Canada filed a resolution calling for News Corporation to appoint an independent chairman, pressing Rupert Murdoch to step down as chairman.

Ted Turner says Rupert Murdoch will have to step down in the wake of the phone-hacking controversy, though Murdoch has consistently denied knowledge of the alleged extent of phone hacking at the News of the World.
Rupert Murdoch appoints his eldest son Lachlan as co-chairman of News Corporation and 21st Century Fox, positioning him as the most likely successor.
Rupert Murdoch hinted that he may share power between his sons Lachlan and James when he eventually hands over control of News Corp, while saying his succession remained an open question.
Lachlan Murdoch, elder son of Rupert Murdoch, is appointed deputy chief operating officer at News Corporation, underlining his position as his father's eventual successor.

events.summary: Rupert Murdoch admitted to the Leveson inquiry that there was a "cover-up" at News International over the phone-hacking scandal and said he was "misinformed and shielded" from what was going on at the News of the World.

Rupert Murdoch told News Corporation's annual general meeting that there were very strict rules and that a person who bought a bugged conversation more than five years earlier was immediately fired, while saying the company would take immediate action if anything came to light.

Rupert Murdoch's London operation, NI Group, disclosed it spent £53.2m on its management and standards committee, bringing total costs from the phone-hacking scandal and News of the World closure to over £300m.
President George W. Bush appoints former Presidents George H.W. Bush and Bill Clinton to lead a joint appeal for emergency donations to victims of the Indian Ocean tsunami.

Trinity Mirror newspapers, including the Daily Mirror, launch a campaign of vilification against Rupert Murdoch and News International over the phone hacking scandal, with front-page headlines such as "Toxic" and "The Wapping Cowboy."
Pressure mounts on Rupert Murdoch to contain the phone hacking scandal within the UK before it spills over into his US media interests, following the closure of the News of the World.
Rupert Murdoch's UK subsidiary told the high court it had found "tens of thousands" of extra emails potentially shedding light on the extent of phone hacking at the News of the World.
President George W. Bush appoints former Presidents George H.W. Bush and Bill Clinton to launch a joint appeal for emergency donations to victims of the Indian Ocean tsunami.
Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation calls in PR firm Edelman to help handle mounting public anger and political pressure over the UK phone-hacking scandal.

A book extract offers reputation-management advice to Rupert Murdoch in the wake of the phone hacking scandal, arguing he can rebuild trust by embracing his inner villain and reforming his media empire.
News Corporation, led by Rupert Murdoch, reported $200m in costs from the News of the World phone hacking scandal, including $87m in the final quarter of 2011 and $108m in the previous quarter.
Detectives are examining an estimated 600 fresh allegations of phone-hacking incidents at Rupert Murdoch's now-closed News of the World after obtaining new evidence from a suspect turned supergrass.
Rupert Murdoch and his son James agree to give evidence to a Commons committee investigating phone hacking after parliament threatens them with imprisonment.

Rupert Murdoch, his son James Murdoch, and Rebekah Brooks are set to face three hours of questions from MPs over phone hacking at News International.

Scotland Yard wants to interview Rupert Murdoch about crime at his UK papers, having contacted the media mogul the previous year but agreeing with lawyers to wait until the end of the phone-hacking trial.
Lawyers for phone-hacking victims accuse directors of Rupert Murdoch's News Group Newspapers of concealing wrongdoing by deliberately deceiving investigators and destroying evidence.

Rupert Murdoch's News International approved a confidential payout to former home secretary David Blunkett over phone-hacking allegations.

Rupert Murdoch's News International agrees out-of-court settlements on 143 of 165 outstanding civil phone-hacking damages cases ahead of a high court hearing.
News Corporation, owned by Rupert Murdoch, made a £100,000 offer of damages to Sienna Miller to settle her phone-hacking case, as disclosed in the high court by its lawyers.

facts.text: On 2003-12-22, Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation completed a £3.8bn deal to acquire DirecTV, giving it control of the largest US satellite pay-TV company.
On 2007-04-04, News Corp shareholders overwhelmingly approved an $11bn asset swap increasing Rupert Murdoch's control, lifting the Murdoch family's stake to 38% from 31%.
On 2011-07-19, Rupert Murdoch expressed regret for News Corporation's involvement in the phone-hacking scandal while insisting he was kept in the dark, during a parliamentary committee hearing.

On 2013-07-01, Rupert Murdoch's media empire officially split into two separately listed companies: News Corp (newspapers, books, Australian pay-TV) and 21st Century Fox (film, TV, European and Asian pay-TV).
On 2016-12-15, Rupert Murdoch's 21st Century Fox formally lodged an £11.7bn bid to take full control of Sky.

On 2017-09-12, the UK culture secretary referred 21st Century Fox's bid to buy the remaining 61% of Sky to the competition regulator on broadcasting standards grounds, opening a new front against Rupert Murdoch.

On 2004-03-16, US media mogul John Malone declared himself a supporter of Rupert Murdoch and his family after building a 9% voting stake in News Corporation, hinting at possible future collaboration between Liberty Media and News Corp.

events.summary: Rupert Murdoch decided to close the News of the World, a decision his chief executive Rebekah Brooks told staff they would understand "in a year."
Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation announces the closure of the News of the World tabloid amid a phone-hacking scandal.
UK prosecutors announce insufficient evidence to bring corporate charges against News UK over phone hacking, effectively clearing Rupert Murdoch's company.
Rupert Murdoch closes the News of the World, Britain's best-selling Sunday newspaper, in an attempt to limit the fallout from the phone-hacking scandal.
Rupert Murdoch attended a Christmas party that drew David Cameron, George Osborne, and other ministers, marking his return to the centre of British power.
James Murdoch ordered the closure of the News of the World amid the phone-hacking scandal, putting 200 jobs at risk, while Rupert Murdoch supported leaving his son in the driving seat.

Prince Alwaleed bin Talal, a major News Corp shareholder, publicly expresses frustration that the phone-hacking scandal is harming the company's reputation while reaffirming his unwavering backing of Rupert Murdoch.

Rebekah Brooks discussed with James Murdoch an internal investigation into phone hacking that might "slam Les, Colin etc" and "vindicate" her position, potentially saving her job but damaging Rupert Murdoch's right-hand man Les Hinton.
Rupert Murdoch asked Rebekah Brooks not to resign on the day the News of the World closed.

Rupert Murdoch outlined plans to move the Wall Street Journal beyond its financial roots and target mainstream competitors such as the New York Times, ahead of completing his $5bn takeover of Dow Jones.

Rupert Murdoch's London operation, NI Group, disclosed it spent £53.2m on its management and standards committee, bringing total costs from the phone-hacking scandal and News of the World closure to over £300m.
Rupert Murdoch appoints his eldest son Lachlan as co-chairman of News Corporation and 21st Century Fox, positioning him as the most likely successor.
Rupert Murdoch said Peter Chernin would probably succeed him as chief executive of News Corporation, while indicating his children were not yet ready to take his place.
The birth of Grace Murdoch, daughter of Rupert Murdoch, is noted as having no immediate effect on the succession question at News Corporation.
Lachlan Murdoch, elder son of Rupert Murdoch, is appointed deputy chief operating officer at News Corporation, underlining his position as his father's eventual successor.
Lachlan Murdoch is expected to take a 50% stake in a joint venture with James Packer to privatise Consolidated Media Holdings, becoming executive chairman.
Rupert Murdoch hinted that he may share power between his sons Lachlan and James when he eventually hands over control of News Corp, while saying his succession remained an open question.
President George W. Bush appoints former Presidents George H.W. Bush and Bill Clinton to launch a joint appeal for emergency donations to victims of the Indian Ocean tsunami.
Rupert Murdoch says his eldest son Lachlan might return to a senior position at News Corporation, more than a year after Lachlan quit as chief operating officer.
Rupert Murdoch took control of US satellite operator DirecTV in a £4.1bn deal, extending his worldwide pay-TV empire to 110 million viewers across four continents.

Rupert Murdoch confirmed he will stand down as chief executive of 21st Century Fox at the end of the month, handing over control to his son James, with the management changes approved by the company's board.
President George W. Bush appoints former Presidents George H.W. Bush and Bill Clinton to launch a joint appeal for emergency donations to victims of the Indian Ocean tsunami.
John Malone becomes the second largest voting shareholder in Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation after increasing his stake to 9%, raising questions about Murdoch's succession plans.

Rupert Murdoch is preparing to step down as chief executive of 21st Century Fox, handing the role to his youngest son James, in a reorganization expected to be ratified at a board meeting as early as next week.

Rupert Murdoch's media empire officially split into two separately listed companies, with the newspaper and book publishing arms and Australian pay-TV assets retaining the News Corp name, while the Fox film and TV businesses and European and Asian pay-TV operations became 21st Century Fox.

Rupert Murdoch falls to his lowest ranking in the MediaGuardian 100, attributed to his completed $5.6bn takeover of Wall Street Journal parent company Dow Jones and his focus on the US financial paper.

News Corp shareholders reacted angrily to reports that James Murdoch could soon be given control of Fox Networks, News Corp's US TV business, with one dissident shareholder calling it a "slap in the face for shareholders."
Rupert Murdoch admitted that he had failed to grasp the significance of the internet, saying most of the industry had been complacent.

Roger Ailes, founder of Fox News and key lieutenant of Rupert Murdoch, signed a new five-year agreement to remain chairman and CEO of Fox News and chairman of Fox Television Stations, and senior adviser to Murdoch.
Rupert Murdoch is to be inducted into the US television academy hall of fame.

existing_events.summary: Pressure mounts on Rupert Murdoch to contain the phone hacking scandal within the UK before it spills over into his US media interests, following the closure of the News of the World.
Rupert Murdoch closes down the News of the World for good amid phone hacking revelations.

Rupert Murdoch apologises at the Leveson inquiry for his shortcomings in the News of the World phone-hacking scandal, admitting there was a "cover-up" at the tabloid and that he had been "misinformed and shielded".
Rupert Murdoch confirms the appointment of his son James Murdoch as chairman and chief executive of News Corporation in Europe and Asia, and Les Hinton as chief executive of Dow Jones.

During a parliamentary debate, Labour MP Tom Watson accused Rupert Murdoch of appointing Rebekah Brooks as chief executive of News International despite knowing she had admitted illegal payments were made to police by the News of the World, and recommended Murdoch be summoned to give evidence to the Commons standards and privileges committee.
Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation admitted liability and issued an unreserved apology in eight phone-hacking lawsuits against the News of the World, aiming to settle cases and contain the scandal.
James Weatherup, a veteran reporter at Rupert Murdoch's News of the World, was arrested in connection with the phone-hacking scandal, complicating News Corp's efforts to contain the affair.

Lord Prescott claims in the House of Lords that the phone-hacking investigation has been extended to the Sunday Times, another title in Rupert Murdoch's media empire, while News International denies that any of its titles other than the News of the World are under investigation.

events.summary: Shareholders, including Hermes and Glass Lewis, campaign to remove Rupert Murdoch as chairman of News Corporation ahead of the company's annual meeting.

Rupert Murdoch faces angry shareholders at News Corp's annual general meeting in Los Angeles, where nearly a quarter of shareholders pledged to vote for the removal of Murdoch, his sons James and Lachlan, and other directors over the phone-hacking scandal.

News Corp shareholders narrowly defeated a proposal to scrap the dual-class share structure that gives the Murdoch family 39.4% voting control, with Rupert Murdoch opening the annual general meeting and endorsing his eldest son Lachlan as co-chairman.

Institutional Shareholder Services criticizes Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation for corporate governance failings, including its dual-class share structure, ahead of the company's relisting in New York.
News Corporation shareholders approve Rupert Murdoch's plan to move the company's headquarters and primary stock market listing from Australia to the US.
The Council of Institutional Investors called on News Corp directors to end the dual-class stock structure that reinforces Rupert Murdoch's dominance over the company.

Rupert Murdoch defended News Corp's history as "stuff of legend" and said he was "personally determined" to clean up the phone hacking scandal at the company's annual shareholder meeting, where he faced the most serious investor revolt in its history.

Lachlan Murdoch, elder son of Rupert Murdoch, is appointed deputy chief operating officer at News Corporation, underlining his position as his father's eventual successor.
Rupert Murdoch's eldest son Lachlan is promoted to non-executive co-chairman of the News Corp board, working alongside his father.
Rupert Murdoch appoints Chase Carey as deputy chairman, president, and chief operating officer of News Corp, replacing Peter Chernin as his second in command.

Rupert Murdoch appoints John Hartigan to replace his son Lachlan as chairman of News Corporation's Australian operations, effective September 1.
President George W. Bush appoints former Presidents George H.W. Bush and Bill Clinton to launch a joint appeal for emergency donations to victims of the Indian Ocean tsunami.
Rupert Murdoch reportedly tried to get his son Lachlan to buy News Limited's Australian business, according to biographer Michael Wolff.

Rupert Murdoch promised that his successor at News Corporation will be chosen by the company's independent directors, while defending his son James's record and not discounting keeping the position in the family.

Rupert Murdoch, James Murdoch, and Rebekah Brooks are invited to appear before the Commons culture select committee over the phone-hacking scandal, with News International stating it will cooperate and await the formal invitation.

Rupert Murdoch and his son James agree to give evidence to a Commons committee investigating phone hacking after parliament threatens them with imprisonment.

events.summary: A lawyer leading the phone-hacking legal challenge says that without "no win, no fee" agreements, Rupert Murdoch's News of the World would still be published, and warns that government proposals to curb such agreements threaten access to justice for hacking victims.

Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation accepted 64 further claims into its compensation scheme for News of the World phone-hacking victims, as more than 70 claimants pursue civil action against News International.
Lawyers for phone-hacking victims accuse directors of Rupert Murdoch's News Group Newspapers of concealing wrongdoing by deliberately deceiving investigators and destroying evidence.
President George W. Bush appoints former Presidents George H.W. Bush and Bill Clinton to lead a joint appeal for emergency donations to victims of the Indian Ocean tsunami.
Rupert Murdoch's News International agrees out-of-court settlements on 143 of 165 outstanding civil phone-hacking damages cases ahead of a high court hearing.
News Corporation, owned by Rupert Murdoch, made a £100,000 offer of damages to Sienna Miller to settle her phone-hacking case, as disclosed in the high court by its lawyers.
Rupert Murdoch's UK subsidiary told the high court it had found "tens of thousands" of extra emails potentially shedding light on the extent of phone hacking at the News of the World.
News Corporation, led by Rupert Murdoch, reported $200m in costs from the News of the World phone hacking scandal, including $87m in the final quarter of 2011 and $108m in the previous quarter.

Rupert Murdoch's News International issued a public apology to eight phone-hacking victims and admitted for the first time that voicemail interception was rife at the News of the World, offering compensation to some of the 24 high-profile figures suing the paper.

News International, Rupert Murdoch's UK newspaper publisher, faces more than 50 new damages claims from alleged victims of News of the World phone hacking, after already settling more than 50 civil actions.

News Corporation agrees to a $139m settlement of a shareholders' lawsuit alleging the board, including chairman Rupert Murdoch, ignored phone hacking at the News of the World, with the settlement to be funded by insurance covering the board.
Rupert Murdoch's News International approved a confidential payout to former home secretary David Blunkett over phone-hacking allegations.

The Crown Prosecution Service ended its four-year phone-hacking investigation without bringing corporate charges against Rupert Murdoch's News UK or criminal cases against Piers Morgan and other former Mirror Group editors, a decision victims' lawyers said they expected to challenge through a formal review.

Rupert Murdoch, James Murdoch, and Rebekah Brooks are invited to appear before the Commons culture select committee over the phone-hacking scandal, with News International stating it will cooperate and await the formal invitation.
MPs issue a summons to compel Rupert Murdoch and his son James to appear before a select committee over the phone-hacking scandal after Rupert Murdoch declined to attend voluntarily.

During a parliamentary debate, Labour MP Tom Watson accused Rupert Murdoch of appointing Rebekah Brooks as chief executive of News International despite knowing she had admitted illegal payments were made to police by the News of the World, and recommended Murdoch be summoned to give evidence to the Commons standards and privileges committee.

Rupert Murdoch, James Murdoch, and Rebekah Brooks are set to face questions from MPs over phone hacking at News International.

The government disclosed that Rupert Murdoch attended a previously undisclosed second meeting with David Cameron at Downing Street in July 2010, shortly after News Corporation launched its bid to take over BSkyB.
Rupert Murdoch and his son James agree to give evidence to a Commons committee investigating phone hacking after parliament threatens them with imprisonment.

A book extract offers reputation-management advice to Rupert Murdoch in the wake of the phone hacking scandal, arguing he can rebuild trust by embracing his inner villain and reforming his media empire.

Rupert Murdoch told News Corporation's annual general meeting that there were very strict rules and that a person who bought a bugged conversation more than five years earlier was immediately fired, while saying the company would take immediate action if anything came to light.
A parliamentary committee report on phone hacking stopped short of declaring Rupert Murdoch unfit to run an international company after Conservative MPs refused to support that conclusion.
Rupert Murdoch, his son James Murdoch, and Rebekah Brooks are set to face three hours of questions from MPs over phone hacking at News International.

Rupert Murdoch's London operation, NI Group, disclosed it spent £53.2m on its management and standards committee, bringing total costs from the phone-hacking scandal and News of the World closure to over £300m.

Rupert Murdoch confirmed he will stand down as chief executive of 21st Century Fox at the end of the month, handing over control to his son James, with the management changes approved by the company's board.

Rupert Murdoch's media empire officially split into two separately listed companies, with the newspaper and book publishing arms and Australian pay-TV assets retaining the News Corp name, while the Fox film and TV businesses and European and Asian pay-TV operations became 21st Century Fox.
